answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and files work each epoch. Without verified work, the bond decays 10%, then 20%, then 40%, a ripple that never reverses: one idle identity falls from 70 to about 30 in three epochs. Auditors recompute decay from the fable ledger each epoch. The k-th fake needs its own 70 bond and decay, since key-bound bonds cover no other identity; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and lose about 39,760 in three epochs. A work-rental ring fails: rented receipts carry another key and are rejected, leaving the epoch hollow. An honest identity files its own work once and keeps its 70.
